Apple has kicked off a new testing cycle, and it's a bit of a surprise: rather than the iPadOS 27.1 update we were expecting, the company has jumped straight to iPadOS 27.2 beta 1.

Apple releases iPadOS 27.2 beta 1 for testing, skipping iPadOS 27.1

iPadOS 27 rolled out to everyone this week, and instead of pushing 27.1 to testers, Apple has gone straight to iPadOS 27.2 developer beta 1.

It's unclear why this update isn't called 27.1. What we do know about iOS 27.1 so far is that it will launch alongside the iPhone Duo.

Perhaps Apple is planning to keep the 27.1 update focused entirely on iPhone Duo-related changes? Either way, we're eager to see what new features iPadOS 27.2 will bring.

Shortly before iPadOS 27 officially launched, Apple removed the 'Suggestions' feature in Messages, as well as the option in the Passwords app that lets the system automatically replace compromised login credentials with new, secure ones.

Apple hasn't said when these features will return, but there's a good chance we'll see them back in this beta.

Another possibility is a redesigned Health app — Apple previously said this app would arrive later this year with new AI-powered enhancements.

Have you installed iPadOS 27.2 beta 1? If you spot anything new, drop us a note in the comments.
